newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN AGREE TO COVER SPONSOR'S LOGOS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN AGREE TO COVER SPONSOR'S LOGOS.

text.p: The Pakistan cricket team on Monday agreed to cover logos bearing cigarette company branding on bats used during their current tour of Australia.

An Australian Health Department spokesman said in a statement the department had been told by the Australian Cricket Board (ACB) that Pakistan had agreed to cover logos bearing the name of the Wills Kings company with white tape during all future matches in Australia.
Pakistan team manager Yawar Saeed said in a statement the team would respect strict Australian laws banning cigarette advertising in sport.

Pakistan were last week told by the Australian government they had until Tuesday, when they play Australia in a World Series Cup limited overs match in Hobart, to cover the logos under strict laws banning cigarette advertising in sport.
The logos were visible during World Series matches against Australia and West Indies last week which were televised around Australia and internationally.
The health department had threatened to refer the matter to Australia's Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions if the Pakistan Cricket Board did not comply with the order.
The ACB also faced fines of up to A$60,000 (US$48,000).
Tobacco adverts are banned at Australian sporting and cultural events unless an exemption is granted. The Formula One Grand Prix motor race in Victoria next March has such an exemption.
